apps.localizedDescription: Standalone multi-provider AI usage monitor for Claude, ChatGPT, Antigravity, Grok, Google AI Studio, and OpenCode Go with secure local credential storage and device pairing.
apps.versionDescription:
Sync Devices link codes are now 12 letters (such as KTQ MPR XDH WAB) instead of 6 digits, because the code also locks the file sent by AirDrop or Quick Share, and anyone who got a copy of that file could otherwise try every 6-digit code. Codes use capital letters only, without I, L or O, so a phone types them on one keyboard and nothing is mistaken for 1 or 0. A device with an older version can still pair over Wi-Fi with a 6-digit code from "Other ways to connect" (turned on in Settings > Sync Options), which never goes into a file.
Settings > Sync Options (under Advanced) has an "Other Ways to Connect" switch. It is off by default, which hides the "Other ways to connect" link in Sync Devices; turn it on to reach the 6-digit code for older app versions and the QR codes. While it is off, the code field ignores digits, so a stray one doesn't switch it to a 6-digit code. The choice is kept on each device.
A new Black appearance (Settings > General > Appearance): the dark theme with pure black backgrounds, sidebar and cards instead of dark grays, which looks deeper and saves battery on OLED screens. Its text is a soft light gray instead of bright white, so it is easier on the eyes; text on colored buttons stays white.
Sync Devices file-sending screens ("Sending by AirDrop" and "Sending by Quick Share") now display a three-step progress card, a "Why AirDrop?" / "Why Quick Share?" card, and side-by-side "Send again via ..." and "Done" buttons.
In Sync Devices, the Enter Link Code letter boxes now match the host link code tiles, and the search countdown reads "If not found within ... seconds, AirDrop / Quick Share will be used instead."
Sync Devices screens and discoverability prompts (Mac AirDrop popup with an amber instruction box, iPhone AirDrop note, Android Quick Share note, and link code screens) now use clearer, consistent wording.
On Android, the Sync Devices "Allow File Access" dialog now explains why access is needed and that only Sync Devices files are opened inside a two-part card, with matching modal title and subtitle sizing.
Dialog close (X) buttons no longer show a "Close" tooltip.
On phones, entering a link code with the on-screen keyboard open now keeps the letter tiles at full size and shortens the vertical gaps between elements instead.
In Sync Devices, the Enter Link Code screen now notes that if the other device isn't on the same network "it uses Quick Share" (or AirDrop on Apple devices), both before typing and during the 10-second countdown, with the method name in bold.
On a Mac, Sync Devices transfer files now show the app's icon and the kind "AI Usage Tracker transfer file" in the share menu and in Finder, instead of a generic icon.
In Settings, the Appearance description now reads "Choose your preferred app theme."
When Sync Devices fails, Try Again now sits at the bottom right in place of Close, styled like Connect. The X at the top still closes the dialog.
On iPhone and iPad, Sync Devices can now move accounts by file too, so an iPhone can sync with a device that isn't on the same network. The accounts go out as one file through the iPhone's share sheet (AirDrop, Messages, Mail, or Save to Files), and when it arrives by AirDrop, or is opened from Files or Mail, while the code shows, the app adds its accounts. As on Android, if the code finds no device on the network, the share sheet opens by itself with the file. Android phones whose Quick Share works with AirDrop (such as recent Pixels and the Galaxy S26) can send to and receive from an iPhone or Mac this way.
In Sync Devices, the screen that shows your link code is now titled "Your Link Code".
When you enter a link code and the other device isn't found on the network, Sync Devices now switches to AirDrop (iPhone and Mac) or Quick Share (Android and Windows) by itself once its 10-second search ends, and opens the share menu with the file of accounts. It switches only when the search itself ends without finding the device, so one that answers late still connects over Wi-Fi. While it looks, a bar counts down the seconds left. The sending screen notes that a VPN on either device can keep them from finding each other on Wi-Fi, and any other reason the search failed is shown as it is.
Settings > Diagnostics now records each Sync Devices step: how the devices connected (link code, QR codes, or a file sent by Quick Share or AirDrop), whether the code was announced on the network and how long the other device took to find it, whether the phone was on Wi-Fi, which network interface the connection used, which transfer files were made, opened or saved, and how the sync ended, with the number of accounts added, updated and skipped or the reason it failed. Link codes, file names and account names are never recorded.
In Sync Devices, the settings option is now called "Also Sync Settings and Layout", and its description no longer mentions the local API.
On Android, Sync Devices no longer stops to ask you to turn on Wi-Fi. It goes straight to the link code, looks for the other device on Wi-Fi or a hotspot, and offers Quick Share when it isn't there.
On the Usage page's 90D view, the back and forward arrows on each card now have tooltips ("Show previous 30 days" and "Show next 30 days"), lined up with the forward arrow's right edge.
On desktop, the Compact button has moved from the top bar to the Dashboard header, beside the % Used / % Left switch, and is now labeled `Compact`.
On desktop and Android, Sync Devices can now move accounts between devices that aren't on the same network, by AirDrop or Quick Share. After you choose Send or Receive and type the code, the sending device looks for the other one on the network; if it isn't there, it sends the accounts by itself as one small file, encrypted with the code, and when the file arrives the receiving device asks whether to add them, with an Add Accounts button. All you do is choose the other device in the share menu, tap Accept on the other side, which the system always asks for, and confirm. On a phone the dialog moves to the top of the screen while it sends, so its steps stay visible above the share sheet. On a Mac the file goes out through the share menu (AirDrop), on Windows through the share panel (Quick Share if installed), and on Android through the share sheet (Quick Share); on Linux you save it to a file. A file that arrives in Downloads is picked up by itself; on Android this needs All files access, which Sync Devices asks for once in a popup while the code shows. On a phone, the receiving screen notes where to let a device on another account share with it (in Quick Share, set "Who can share with you" to "Everyone for 10 Minutes" on Android; set AirDrop to "Everyone for 10 Minutes" on iPhone), since apps can't change it. On a Mac or Windows PC a popup explains the same, with a button to the AirDrop window (Mac) or Nearby sharing (Windows). Only a file that arrives while the code shows is used, it opens only with that code, and it is deleted once used. On the receiving device, a small link opens a file by hand if it ever isn't picked up. The app isn't offered to open any other kind of file.
The status bar at the top of the Dashboard has larger text, on desktop and on phones. On a phone, the "Next reset" line now always sits in its own gray row under a divider, not only when a limit is running low.
The Usage page's key (Measured, Estimated, No data, Reset) has larger text, matching the Dashboard's status bar, on desktop and on phones. On desktop the key box is now as tall as the status bar, and on narrow phones it stays on one line.
Sync Devices takes fewer steps: after choosing Send or Receive, the receiving device shows its link code at once and the sending device asks for it. Typing the last letter connects without pressing Connect, and once connected the sending device sends straight away instead of asking "Send to the other device?". A 6-digit code for a device with an older version, and the QR code, are under "Other ways to connect", which is hidden unless you turn it on in Settings. A failed pairing now says "Pairing Failed" in the heading, with a green Try Again button.
In Settings, the Menu Bar Labels switch description now reads "Show labels below icons in bottom bar."
The Sync Devices link code screens have a new look: the code shows as large letter tiles in two rows, each three letters, a small gap and three more, with a bar counting down to when it expires, the code you type fills matching tiles, a pulsing dot shows while it looks for the other device, and the file transfer screens show each step with a tick as it's done.
Error messages in dialogs (Sync Devices, Add Account, groups, alerts, Google AI Studio) now stay for 10 seconds instead of 6, and have an X in the top right corner to close them sooner.
On phones and tablets, dialogs (such as Sync Devices when it finishes) no longer show a purple outline around the whole dialog or around a button. That outline marks keyboard focus, and a touch screen has no Tab key to move it.
When Sync Devices fails, the reason now stays on screen until you close it with its X, press Back or press Try Again. Before, it disappeared after 10 seconds and left "The reason is below" pointing at nothing.
On desktop, the usage bars in compact account cards are now centered in the card, with the same space above and below. Before, they sat slightly low.
When you type a link code, it now fills two rows of three-letter groups, matching the code on the other device.
On the Usage page, switching between 7D, 30D and 90D no longer dims the cards for a moment; the old charts stay until the new ones are drawn.
On Android, a phone that shares its hotspot while also connected to Wi-Fi can now enter the link code of a device that joined its hotspot. Before, pairing failed with "The link to the other device broke" unless that phone showed the code instead.
Removed the "Received a file but nothing happened? Open it" button from the Sync Devices link code screen.
